definitions.metric_granularity: document; distinct doc_id in ranked order, truncated to top_k
definitions.semantic_recall: recall_at_k against human relevant_doc_ids; denominator is the number of distinct gold docs, not K; not ANN recall
definitions.mrr: mean reciprocal rank of the first gold doc at doc rank r <= top_k; no gold in Top-K contributes 0; denominator is evaluated queries
definitions.rrf: sum over arms of 1 / (k + rank), rank starts at 1, k=60; raw dense/sparse scores are never added
definitions.reranker_pool: the historical ⑥-B RRF Top-10 candidate identities for the same query; text is fetched live from PostgreSQL; the dense and sparse arms are not re-run
definitions.reranker_score: raw cross-encoder logit with activation=identity; higher is better; only relative order is meaningful and it is not comparable with cosine similarity or ts_rank_cd
definitions.reranker_order: rerank_score descending, then pre-rerank rank, then (chunk_strategy, chunk_id)
definitions.no_gold_handling: reciprocal rank 0.0 and no fabricated gold document
definitions.precision_ndcg: not computed: the labels are not exhaustive, so unlabelled non-gold positions cannot be treated as true negatives

latency.statistical_basis: 30 timed queries, one deterministic rerank pass each; nearest-rank percentiles; no confidence interval; model load and warm-up are excluded from per-query latency

limitations: The four arms (dense, sparse_or, sparse_and, rrf) are reused from the Phase 6B artifact, not re-run against PostgreSQL in Phase 7B. Their raw hits are independently re-scored and the RRF formula is re-checked, but this is offline replay.
The RRF+Reranker arm reranks the historical RRF Top-10 identities; those candidates are not regenerated by a live dense/sparse query in this run.
Recall cannot increase over RRF because the reranker sees the same Top-10 pool; only ordering metrics (MRR, Hit@1) can change.
The corpus has one chunk per document, so chunk-level and document-level candidate sets coincide here.
The 30 queries are English; Chinese and mixed-language reranking are not evaluated.
The embedding model and the reranker were not loaded in the same process; combined-memory behaviour is not measured, so this run does not claim to solve it.
Host Python execution may differ from the pinned container environment; Docker was not used for this run and the container path is unverified.
The full pytest suite was not run because the host torch/transformers stack has a known native crash on an embedding integration test; only module-level tests ran.
Dependency versions on the host differ from the exact pins in pyproject.toml; that drift is not resolved or verified here.
Latency is CPU-only, single-process, sequential and warm. No GPU, scale, concurrency or cross-machine reproducibility claim is made.
Precision and nDCG are not reported because non-gold labels are not exhaustive.
A database failure was exercised with unit-level connection stubs, not by stopping the live PostgreSQL server during this benchmark.
